$Comment: What Enchanter Orrin pays for the Unmaking Rites, his daily. The daily's whole payout is this
one table, so retune the daily here and the quest file never changes.
A CLAIM TABLE, never a station table. It rolls when the player collects the reward from the
quest log, with only the player in context: no piece of gear, no table, no tool. That is why
every roll here reads the PLAYER alone (Enchanting level and luck through hytale:stat) and
none carries a Trigger or a gear condition. The table's own station tables (Disenchant_Void
and the rest) gate their rolls on the placed piece's level and so can never pay from a claim;
this file is the claim-side twin of those finds, sized for one day rather than one ritual.
ROLLS EVALUATE INDEPENDENTLY. Every roll whose Chance passes pays out on the same claim, so a
good day hands over several at once. The first roll always pays, and each one after it is a
bonus on top. Chance is a percentage, 0 to 100; a roll with no Chance always fires. Count and
CountMax together are a range, rolled per grant.
THE FIRST ROLL IS A LADDER, which is what makes the daily grow with the enchanter instead of
paying a beginner and a veteran the same handful. Its Factors are summed into one score and the
Floors are read against that score; floors are NOT cumulative, so the highest one reached wins
and only its Grants fire. Two things feed the score, weighted equally: the Enchanting level, so
the rites pay better as the skill grows, and Enchanting luck, so a luck-heavy tree pays here as
well as at the table. Each floor pays Enchanting XP through a Rewards entry (the Mmo_Xp kind:
Skill plus Amount) and a little Life essence on the side.
UNITS, the one trap worth knowing. Both channels are read as WHOLE NUMBERS: MMO_StationYield_ENCHANTING
stores whole percent points, so a fully claimed Enchanting tree reads near a hundred rather
than near one, and MMO_Level_ENCHANTING is a level, not a fraction. The floors below are
therefore written on a scale of roughly 0 to 250. Never swap these two leaves for the
mmoskilltree:station_luck aggregate: that one returns a FRACTION, which would shift every floor
by a factor of a hundred.
The three chance rolls carry a Cue, the celebration id a roll may author beside its Grants. It
fires only when the grants beside it genuinely paid out; Rare_Find is the everyday chime the
MMO jar ships as a toast. All the odds and floors here are opening balance.
Name: Mmo_Enchanter_Rites

Rolls.$Comment: Always pays, and pays more the further along the enchanter is. Floor 0 is what somebody who has only just earned a table receives; the top floor wants a high level and a full luck tree together rather than one alone.

Floors.$Comment: The starting tier, reachable by anybody, since a score of 0 always passes.
An enchanter past the early levels, or one who has claimed a few luck rewards.
A committed enchanter: a solid level with real luck investment behind it.
The top of the ladder, needing both halves near their ceiling rather than one alone.

Rolls.$Comment: The everyday bonus, roughly two days in five: a thread of Void essence, the thing the table finds in good gear.
The uncommon bonus, roughly one day in ten: a Disenchanter's Draught, which hurries the ritual along for a few minutes.
The rare pull, roughly one day in fifty at no luck and one in twenty-five with a full tree: a Voidheart. Luck acts on the odds here, not on the count, because a heart is a yes or a no.
